text:
alex_sales: Heads up — AcmeCorp POC hit flaky streaming. Their frontend reports JSON parse errors mid-stream, sometimes connection closes after ~3-10s. Can we swarm?

acme_sre: Repro steps — using our React SSE client, we see partial chunks like '{"delta":"..."' then connection drops. No obvious HTTP 5xx. No body after close.

sam_engineer: Got it. Two suspects: 1) intermediate proxy truncating chunked transfer, 2) server closing keep-alive due to rate limits or idle timeout. Can you paste the raw client console logs and the request headers?

acme_sre: Console shows: "EventSource failed: Unexpected end of input" and network panel shows response as text/event-stream with Transfer-Encoding: chunked. Headers: Authorization, Accept: text/event-stream, Connection: keep-alive. No Content-Length.

maya_se: Quick triage: ask them to try curl -N to reproduce and capture exact bytes. Example to run locally:
```bash
curl -v -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer $RW_KEY" \n  -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/streaming \n  -d '{"model":"rwd-large-1","stream":true,"prompt":"hi"}'
```
This will show if the server closes mid-event.

sam_engineer: Also check for proxies/load balancers that buffer and enforce a max chunk size. Our runtime streams small SSE chunks — if an edge concatenates or drops final newline, browser EventSource can fail parsing. Ask them to look for any nginx/ingress timeouts.

alex_sales: Acme says they use a managed gateway with 30s idle timeout. They get drops sooner though.

maya_se: Two quick server-side checks we can run from our side: enable streaming debug mode for their API key so we emit extended frame logs and x-rw-trace-id headers. I can toggle `stream_diagnostics=true` on their tenant — that will add logs in the trace: server_sent_bytes, last_chunk_size. Want me to turn it on?

acme_sre: Please do. Also they asked about retry/backoff behavior and pricing if we suggest higher QPS for Dedicated.

zoe_account: Noted — will follow up on pricing. For now we need root cause.

sam_engineer: Turned on diagnostics for their key. Trace id: trace_176714. You can repro and paste trace id here. We'll check logs for partial chunk termination.

deploy-bot: deploy completed: streaming-runtime v2.14 -> us-east-1 at 2026-03-20T14:45:12Z :white_check_mark:

sam_engineer: On runtime side, also confirm they are not using gzip compression at the gateway. Compression + chunked streaming often causes early flush behavior. If gzip is on, ask them to disable it for the SSE endpoint.

acme_sre: Ran curl -N, attached raw output (shortened):
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/event-stream
Transfer-Encoding: chunked

data: {"delta":"Hello"}

data: {"delta":" wor"}

[data cut off here]
```
Connection closed by peer.

sam_engineer: That looks like the server (or a proxy) closed before final 'data' chunk. From our traces: stream_176714 shows last_chunk_size=24 then stream closed with code 0 on our side — which usually indicates the client closed or the upstream dropped. Can you confirm their gateway logs for TCP RST?

maya_se: Workaround while we investigate: 1) client can buffer and tolerate partial last chunk by concatenating until a full JSON object is received, 2) switch to our WebSocket streaming endpoint which is less sensitive to chunk boundaries. If they need a fast fix, try WebSocket.

alex_sales: Acme prefers minimal changes to their frontend. They asked if Redwood can add a small keepalive comment every 10s to prevent some gateways from closing. Is that something we can toggle per-tenant?

sam_engineer: We have keepalive pings but not per-tenant toggle yet. I can enable it for their key as an experiment (sends ":\n" comment SSE every 8s). Will do and report back in ~15m.

zoe_account: I'll note this change and update the SOW timeline. Also follow-up on Dedicated pricing options for higher concurrency.

acme_sre: Thanks — will rerun reproducible curl after keepalive enabled and paste trace id.

sam_engineer: Keepalive enabled for their tenant (trace flag). New trace base: trace_176714_run2. If they still see parse errors, capture http raw bytes and share. Also mention whether they're using the native EventSource or a polyfill — polyfills behave differently on truncated events.

alex_sales: Great. I'll coordinate with Acme and push them to test WebSocket fallback if needed.

acme_sre: Running now. If this doesn't work, we'll try WS.

maya_se: One more note — if they plan to move to Dedicated, some idle timeout behaviors change (edge timeouts are removed in certain private deployments). That might be relevant to their decision tree.

zoe_account: I'll add a pricing note and schedule a deep-dive call tomorrow 10am PT if keepalive doesn't resolve it.

sam_engineer: Thanks everyone. Follow-up once we have trace_176714_run2 logs from customer.
